kindExtra: Key shape for this task: `text` on `attack` (`true`); two `some` items with `timeNear` on `window` (start and end, tolMin 3); `some` items on `sources`: one matching `192\.0\.2\.` with `attempts` within 5% of the planted count (num bounds), one matching `203\.0\.113\.77` within 5%; a hand-written `hidden/accounts.test.js` (add a second `tests` check, weight 3) that asserts `compromised` equals exactly the six planted ids as a set (any extra or missing id fails) and holds no `qa-` id; `number` on `attemptedNotCompromised` (tolPct 5); `some` on `legitimateExcluded` matching `198\.51\.100\.10|load test|qa-`; `text` items on the prose or `actions`: the clock offset (`UTC-5|five hours|5 ?h|local time|clock|offset` near `gw-b`), `203\.0\.113\.77` named as not allowlisted (`not (in|on) the allowlist|outside|not ours`), an action with `block|deny` and `192\.0\.2\.0/24`, an action with `reset|revoke` and `24 ?h(ours)?`, an action with `MFA|multi-?factor|2FA`; `evidence` groups (min 3): a `login_fail` line from an attack IP, a `token_issued` line for a compromised id, a `qa-` line from 198.51.100.10, a line of `config/allowlist.yaml`; `evidencePrecision` min 0.5. No wording is required for the narrative; the set and the numbers carry the score.

facts.answer: 203.0.113.77 is not ours. Our office range stops at .63; that address is outside it and not on the allowlist.
For every account the attacker logged into: force a password reset, revoke its tokens, and email the owner within 24 hours.
Yes, block 192.0.2.0/24 outright. Nothing legitimate comes from there.

brief: Phase: log analysis. Role: security (on-call security engineer). Folder: `logs/gw-a.jsonl` and `logs/gw-b.jsonl`, about 2,500 JSON lines each from two auth gateway nodes for one night (`ts`, `node`, `event` in login_attempt, login_ok, login_fail, mfa_challenge, mfa_ok, token_issued; `account`, `src_ip`, `ua`, `reason`), with normal traffic all night from many addresses; `logs/README.md` with the field meanings and one line saying node gw-b logs in local time (UTC-5) because of a known config bug, with a ticket id; `config/allowlist.yaml` with the office and VPN egress ranges 203.0.113.0/26 and 198.51.100.8/29; `notes/oncall.md` with the alert text and the on-call's first guess ('probably the load test again?'); `notes/load-test-schedule.md`: a QA load test runs nightly 02:00 to 02:20 UTC from 198.51.100.10 with 50 test accounts named qa-*; `accounts/directory.csv` (account id, display name, MFA on or off, last password change). Plant: an attack from 01:10 to 02:35 UTC from 192.0.2.0/24 (about 1,800 attempts spread over the range) and the single address 203.0.113.77 (about 400 attempts; it is outside the allowlisted /26, which ends at .63), one user agent throughout, one or two attempts per account over hundreds of accounts; exactly six compromised accounts: login_fail from an attack address, then login_ok and token_issued from an attack address, MFA off in the directory; about 640 distinct accounts attempted and not compromised; three accounts with login_ok from an attack address followed by mfa_challenge and no mfa_ok (no session, not compromised); two accounts with a login_ok inside the window from their own usual address seen earlier that evening (not compromised); the load test producing about 600 login_fail lines on qa-* accounts from 198.51.100.10 at 02:00 to 02:20 (the decoy: scheduled, allowlisted, excluded); gw-b timestamps five hours behind, so the window is wrong until corrected. The request asks whether this was an attack, which accounts the attacker actually logged into, when it started and ended (UTC), where it came from, what to block or reset, the document at the given path ending with the JSON block, and log lines cited as `path:line`. The request must not mention the clock bug, the load test, the allowlist boundary or MFA. The lazy answer says the load test caused the alert and recommends nothing; the copy answer pastes login_fail counts; both must fail. The three scripted facts (whether .77 is ours, the reset and notification policy, whether the /24 may be blocked) are not in the folder; the reference asks for them and the actions use them.
